reason: The cited evidence (E1) directly supports the first three premises by reporting the successful fabrication of a bimodal RAFM steel with nanoscale precipitates, high strength, and high ductility linked to mobile dislocations and subgrains. However, it provides no data on the proposed dislocation-transfer mechanism across subgrain boundaries, nor any testing under high-temperature or irradiation conditions, leaving the last two premises unsupported by the cited passage.
premises: A bimodal microstructure with nanoscale precipitates and fine grains/subgrains can be produced in RAFM steel by a modified thermomechanical process.
This microstructure yields high strength and high ductility simultaneously.
High ductility is attributed to a high mobile dislocation density in ferrite and subgrain formation in tempered martensite.
Nanoscale precipitates and subgrains mediate dislocation motion to delay strain localization and crack initiation.
These mechanisms will remain effective under fusion-relevant conditions (>600 °C, irradiation).
